title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Zimbabwe: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Zimbabwe: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Zimbabwe: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Organizing palliative care, legal capacity planning, disability social security claims, and estate readiness while navigating a serious or terminal illness in Zimbabwe involves coordinating medical care, Powers of Attorney, valid wills under Chapter 6:06, NSSA invalidity benefits, and tax records. Because Ministry of Health and Child Care (mohcc.gov.zw under maintenance), Judicial Service Commission (jsc.org.zw), Civil Registry (rg.gov.zw), Foreign Affairs (zimfa.gov.zw), and NSSA (nssa.org.zw) portals currently present external maintenance pages, redirects, or TLS failures, this guide cites live websites for Island Hospice and Healthcare, ZIMRA, Veritas Zimbabwe, ZimLII, and HCCH.

steps.title: Palliative Support, Medical Records, and Mental Capacity
steps.html:
• Contact Island Hospice and Healthcare in Harare or Bulawayo for multidisciplinary home-based palliative nursing, pain and symptom management, family counseling, and clinical social care [1][2].
  • Work with attending clinicians and national palliative care networks to secure continuous access to prescribed pain-relief medicines across hospital and community settings [1][2].
  • Request comprehensive specialist clinical summaries, diagnostic records, and functional capacity evaluations early, and review curatorship safeguards under the Mental Health Act [Chapter 15:12] and SI 2022-205 regulations if progressive illness impairs legal or financial decision-making [7].

steps.title: Powers of Attorney and Formal Will Execution
steps.html:
• Execute a written Power of Attorney under the Powers of Attorney Act [Chapter 8:09] while legal capacity holds; for property or deeds registry transactions, ensure execution satisfies Deeds Registries Act witnessing standards (notary public, legal practitioner, or justice of the peace per section 78 reform guidance) [6][8].
  • Draft and execute a valid written will in accordance with the Wills Act [Chapter 6:06] (testator capacity, written document signed at the foot in the simultaneous presence of two competent witnesses) and keep safe-custody records aligned with the Master of the High Court under the Administration of Estates Act [Chapter 6:01] [3][4][5][6].

steps.title: NSSA Invalidity Benefits and Beneficiary Designations
steps.html:
• Contributors unable to continue regular employment due to permanent incapacity should prepare medical board documentation to apply for an Invalidity Pension or Grant with the National Social Security Authority (NSSA) under the National Social Security Authority Act [Chapter 17:04] and SI 2024-099 [9].
  • Update dependant and nominee records across workplace pension funds, NSSA membership files, and life insurance policies.

steps.title: Asset, Deeds, and ZIMRA Tax Record Preparation
steps.html:
• Consolidate national identity documents, marriage records, property title deeds, banking mandates, and Business Partner tax numbers with the Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA) [10][11].
  • Record clear information on any principal family residence, vehicle, or specified assets relevant to future Estate Duty and Capital Gains Tax administration [10][11].

steps.title: Cross-Border Document Authentication (Non-Apostille)
steps.html:
• Zimbabwe is not a Contracting Party to the HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so Apostille certificates do not replace embassy authentication [12].
  • Powers of attorney, certified medical reports, and civil status documents prepared for use outside Zimbabwe require notarization, High Court authentication, Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation, and destination embassy legalization [12].
